Summary of the iteration history of blvim

Source: R/blvim_history.R
summary.blvim_history.Rd

Summarises the iteration history of the gradient algorithms of blvim(), as returned by sim_history(), for one model or for a collection of models.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'blvim_history'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary_blvim_history'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

a data frame of class blvim_history produced by sim_history()

...

additional parameters (not used currently)

x

an object of class summary_blvim_history produced by summary.blvim_history()

Value

an object of class summary_blvim_history and list with the following elements:

  • runs: a data frame with one row per run and columns sim (index of the model in the collection, 1 for a single model), iterations, initial_potential, final_potential, final_gap, rate, reductions, min_step, initial_active and final_active (number of active destinations), face_changes (number of changes of the number of active destinations), last_change (iteration of the last face change, NA without change), final_min_U (smallest rescaled attractiveness of the final configuration), vanishing (whether a destination may be slowly vanishing) and on_face (whether the final configuration is on a face of the simplex);

  • collection: whether the history describes a collection of models.

Details

For each run, the summary gives the number of iterations, the initial and final potentials, the final duality gap, the estimated convergence rate of the duality gap, the total number of step reductions in the line search, the smallest accepted step, and the evolution of the active destinations. The convergence rate is the factor by which the gap is multiplied at each iteration, estimated on the last iterations (at most 20): a rate close to one denotes a slow linear convergence.

The projected gradient ascent moves on the faces of the simplex: a destination vanishes when its rescaled attractiveness becomes zero, and can come back later. Each change of the number of active destinations is a face change. The duality gap often decreases quickly only once the ascent stays on the face of its final configuration, that is after the last face change. A final configuration whose smallest rescaled attractiveness is below \(10^{-5}\) is on a face of the simplex. Conversely, when the final configuration is not on a face but its smallest rescaled attractiveness decreased by more than a factor 10 over the last half of the iterations, a destination may be slowly vanishing, which slows down the convergence.

See also

sim_history(), grid_sim_history(), autoplot.blvim_history()

Examples

distances <- french_cities_distances[1:15, 1:15] / 1000
production <- rep(1, 15)
attractiveness <- rep(1, 15)
model <- blvim(distances, production, 1.5, 1 / 50, attractiveness,
  algorithm = "gradient", bipartite = FALSE,
  control = blvim_gradient_control(history = TRUE)
)
summary(sim_history(model))
#> 
#> ── Iteration history of a gradient ascent ──
#> 
#> • 37 iterations, potential from -13.88252 to -13.42567.
#> • Final duality gap: 1.425e-05.
#> • Convergence rate of the duality gap: 0.5295 per iteration.
#> • Line search: 15 step reductions, smallest accepted step 0.005049.
#> • Active destinations: from 15 to 13, 2 face changes, the last one at iteration
#> 26.
#> • The final configuration is on a face of the simplex.
